back-to-herman-talking-to-arnold-again.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
back-to-herman-talking-to-arnold-again.text: It good to see you, [player name], but many things I have to do with lovely fresh monkfish you bring me earlier.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Do you like my magic Zombies? Feel free to kill them, there's plenty more where these came from!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: Hello. I need your help with something...

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Oho? Very well, young man, what can I do for you?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: The Piscatoris Fishing Colony, somewhere north of the Gnome Stronghold, is under attack by sea trolls, and they've sent me to ask for an army.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: An army, heh? But I haven't GOT an army!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: They said you might lend us some of your zombies.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: What? This is a combat training facility, not a library! My magic zombies are not for loan.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: So you can't help the Colony?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: I'm jolly well not lending them an army! If I did that for you, I'd have to do that for everyone, and I'd never get a moment's peace again!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: So what should I tell the Colony? They've got to give up all their work because you won't help?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Actually that does seem rather harsh...

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: Now, you mustn't breathe a word of this to Zavistic or Disentor upstairs, but I know a man who could help you get an army.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: Great! Is he a Guild wizard too?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: No, his work is completely different. He's a necromancer.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: Necromancy? I don't want anything to do with that!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: He's not going to have you doing any of the actual spellcasting for it. You'll probably just have to collect some weird item from him and take it to the Colony.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.player: I don't know if I still want to do this.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone.text: If you don't want to continue the quest, just walk away and think no more about it. But I'm sure you won't have to do anything evil or unnatural yourself.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.player: Enough of this - I'm off.

steps.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
steps.text: Understandable. But if you ever change your mind, just come and ask me.

options.text: I'll see what the necromancer needs me to do.

steps.player: I'll see what the necromancer needs me to do.

steps.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
steps.text: Excellent. His name's Malignius Mortifer. You'll find him somewhere south of Falador.

steps.player: Can't I ask a different necromancer? There's one not so far away.

steps.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
steps.text: Hah! Necromancers aren't helpful people. I don't know of many - most guild wizards won't have anything to do with their practices. I think Malignius will help only because he loves showing off his powers.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.player: You said you knew a man who could help me save the Piscatoris Fishing Colony.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: Oh yes. Now, you mustn't mention this to Zavistic or Distentor, but he's a necromancer.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.player: Necromancy? I don't want anything to do with that!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: Do you like my magic Zombies? Feel free to kill them, there's plenty more where these came from!

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: [player name]? Have you spoken to Malignius Mortifer?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.speaker: Wizard Frumscone
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-f.text: He'll probably still be wandering around south of Falador whenever you do want to speak to him.

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.speaker: Herman Caranos
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.text: [player name] - have you brought an army?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.player: Wizard Frumscone wouldn't help, but he told me where I could find a wizard who might help. I have to look for him just south of Falador.
By the way, where's the Wise Old Man gone?

talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.speaker: Herman Caranos
talking-to-wizard-frumscone-talking-to-h.text: He said he'd be back in a minute. But never mind him - go to Falador and talk to this wizard!

talking-to-malignius-mortifer.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
talking-to-malignius-mortifer.text: So, [player name], your curiosity leads you to speak to me?

options.text: Who are you and what are you doing here?

steps.player: Who are you and what are you doing here?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: I am the great Malignius Mortifer, wielder of strange and terrible powers. These lowly followers of mine are dedicated students of the magical arts. Their business is to follow me and learn all they can.

steps.player: They don't look very tough.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You may believe that, but even if you strike one down, another will rise up within minutes.

steps.player: Yeah, right.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Each of my followers is a master of his chosen element. His life becomes bound to that element in a way you could not hope to understand.

steps.player: And what do you do?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: I am mastering a branch of magic that few dare to attempt: Necromancy! The fools in the Guild of Wizards shun anyone who practices this art, but there are a few in this land who know the rudiments.
If Zogre Flesh Eaters has been completed:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Grayzag, Invrigar, Sithik... Even Melzar studied the methods of necromancy, until an accident affected his mind. Now his spells tend to result in...
If Zogre Flesh Eaters hasn't been completed:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Grayzag and Invrigar... Even Melzar studied the methods of necromancy, until an accident affected his mind. Now his spells tend to result in...

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: ... well, let us simply say that he does NOT raise armies of undead minions.

steps.prompt: What would you like to say?

steps.player: Is this like Summoning? Can you teach me?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: The obscure magical art of necromancy has nothing to do with Summoning.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Through necromancy, I may resurrect the bodies of those who have fallen, and bend them to my will, and even command them to tell me hidden knowledge.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: I shall not pass on my secrets lightly to any passer-by!

steps.player: Even a mighty hero like me?

steps.text: If the player isn't wearing equipment aligned with Guthix, Saradomin, or Zamorak:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Perhaps one day you shall learn ways to summon creatures to your side, but my own work is of a different sort.
If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Guthix:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Deluded lover of Guthix, you will get no secrets from me!
If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Saradomin:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Saradominist fool, you will get no secrets from me!
If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Zamorak:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Although I note your respect for our Lord Zamorak, I am afraid the subtle secrets of necromancy must remain beyond your grasp.

steps.player: What happened to Melzar?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: The forces required to wield power over the dead are very difficult to control. Melzar's concentration slipped, and his spell rebounded upon him.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Although he did not die, his mind broke. Now he dwells amidst the beasts that fill his strange home, and when he attempts to do magic he gets... amusing results.

options.text: Why do you keep making fungi appear?

steps.player: Why do you keep making fungi appear?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Necromancy is... still not fully understood. So few people dare to study it. Although my spells usually raise whichever undead creature I desire, they sometimes misfire. As Melzar has learnt!

steps.player: Thanks, I'll be off now.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: I am sure your curiosity will eventually draw you to speak to me again, [player name].

options.text: I need help with saving a fishing colony.

steps.player: I need help with saving a fishing colony.

steps.text: If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Saradomin:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Not when you're dressed like that! I don't help Saradominist filth!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Hahaha! You want MY help? HAHAHA!

steps.player: ... um... The Piscatoris Fishing Colony needs an army to defend them against attacking trolls.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: And of all the people in the world, you came to ask ME? HAHAHA!

steps.player: ... um... pretty please?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Oh, I'll help! I'll give you GOOD help!

steps.player: ... um... thanks, I think...

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: An army, eh? I can raise you a lovely army of the undead skeletal magi! That'd be just right, wouldn't it?

steps.player: I'm not going to have to do anything... evil, am I?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: No, I'll keep the fun bits for myself. You'll just have to get a few things for me.

steps.player: Alright - what do you need?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Firstly, I need 7 bones, the normal sort you get from people and small monsters.
With no bones in inventory:
If the player already has the bones:

steps.player: I have some here!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Hah! And I thought only necromancers and jogres carried bones around with them! Very well, hand 'em over.

steps.player: What should I do now for the quest?

steps.text: (Continues below)

steps.player: About those enchanted secateurs again...

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: What now, [player name], can't you just leave me alone to practice my art?

options.text: Can I get another set of enchanted secateurs?

steps.player: Can I get another set of enchanted secateurs?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Well I guess it's your lucky day! Since your last visit I've been thinking, I never use my enchanted secateurs anymore, I could sell them to you, if you like.

steps.player: That's great!
How much would they cost?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: I could let you have them for a mere 40,000 gp.

steps.player: 40,000! That's outrageous!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Well, that's my price. If you change your mind, you can come back and talk to me. Good day.

options.text: That's too expensive for me I'm afraid.

steps.player: That's too expensive for me I'm afraid.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Well, that's my price. If you change your mind, you can come back and talk to me. Good day.

steps.player: Ok, great.

steps.text: If the player has at least 40,000 coins, and enough inventory space:
magic secateurs

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: A pleasure doing business with you, [player name].
If the player has at least 40,000 coins, but no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You don't have room to hold them. Stop wasting my time.
If the player does not have at least 40,000 coins:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You don't have 40,000 gp with you! Do you take me for a fool?

steps.player: Sorry, I didn't realise. I'll have to visit a bank.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Fine, I might see you later then.

steps.player: Sorry to have bothered you.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: That's ok, I shouldn't have been so abrupt with you.

options.text: Where can I get clothes like those?

steps.player: Where can I get clothes like those?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Bah! Our garments are an outward sign of our dominance of the magical arts. You cannot simply buy them in a shop!

steps.player: What happens if I kill you and take them?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Try it and see!

steps.player: How about if you teach me enough about magic so I can wear those clothes too?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: How about if I turn you into a mushroom to make you stop bothering me?
The player is transformed into a mushroom.

steps.player: MMMmmph!

options.text: What was it you said you'd need to help me save the Colony?

steps.player: What was it you said you'd need to help me save the Colony?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Bones! I need bones, the normal sort you get from humans and small monsters. If you're having trouble, go to the highwaymen just north of here - they've got bones!

steps.player: Oh yes, how could I have forgotten?

options.text: Where can I get clothes like those?

talking-to-malignius-mortifer-giving-bon.player: I have some bones for you.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Good. Now I need [Amount] more.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Excellent!

steps.player: What should I do now for the quest?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: From the bones you have given me, I shall make bone seeds. These will contain the essence of your army. But you will need some way to carry the seeds.

steps.player: What had you in mind?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You must go to the Crafting Guild to ask the advice of the master crafters. There are quite a few of them there, and one of them's sure to help.
If the player has a brown apron:
If the player does not have a brown apron

steps.player: I doubt they'll let me in there without a brown apron.

steps.text: Brown apron

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Here, take this one.

steps.player: Thanks!

options.text: Could you spare me a brown apron?
options.condition: If the player lost their apron:

steps.player: Can you spare me a brown apron so I can go to the Crafting Guild to ask the master crafters about transporting bone seeds?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Yes, yes.

steps.player: Thanks!

options.text: What am I meant to be doing for the Colony?

steps.player: What am I meant to be doing for the Colony?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Is there something wrong with your memory? I told you to go to the Crafting Guild to ask the master crafters for advice on transporting bone seeds.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.text: Hello, and welcome to the Crafting Guild. Accomplished crafters from all over the land come here to use our top notch workshops.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.player: Can you tell me anything about transporting bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.text: Bone seeds? What are bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-a.player: A necromancer is going to bind the essence of an undead army into some bone seeds for me if I can get a container to carry them in.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: Can you tell me anything about transporting bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Woah dude! That's, like, some seriously maximum stuff you're talking.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: But do you know what I should carry them in?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Yeah, you just need a pot with a lid. Do you know how to make pot lids?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: Yes, a woman called Tassie taught me.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Tassie Slipcast? She's one groovy lady.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: Yes, yes, very nice. So if I get a pot with a lid, I'll be able to carry bone seeds safely in it?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: Yeah, yeah. You need to chill out more, dude.

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.player: What was it you said I needed for transporting bone seeds?

talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.speaker: Master Crafter
talking-to-a-master-crafter-talking-to-t.text: A pot with a lid. Nothing more, nothing less.

options.text: I've spoken to the master crafter...

steps.player: I've spoken to the master crafter about a container for transporting bone seeds.

steps.text: If the player is wearing equipment aligned with Saradomin:

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: You can take that Saradominist attire off before you try speaking to me about your quest again!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Ah, excellent. HAHAHA! Have you got such a container?
If the player doesn't have a pot and pot lid:

steps.player: No, I haven't got one.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Then get one!
If the player has a pot and pot lid:

steps.player: Yes, I have it here.

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: I have raised you an army and bound them into bone seeds for you!

steps.player: ... um... Thanks!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Don't mention it, it was fun! HAHAHA!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Now I will seal the seeds into your pot.
Bone seeds

steps.player: Thank you. So what do I do with them?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Take the pot to the Colony and open it! HAHAHA! Just don't open it before you get there.

steps.player: Suppose I - ahem - need another one later?

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: Bring me another of these pots with a lid and I will give you more bone seeds.
Malignius unexpectedly casts a spell on you.
Malignius unexpectedly casts a spell on you!

steps.speaker: Malignius Mortifer
steps.text: HAHAHA!
The player is teleported to the Fishing Colony

options.text: Where can I get clothes like those?

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Franklin Caranos
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: Herman tells me you've been fetching us an army.

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Franklin Caranos
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: Interesting. I didn't know magic could do that.

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.player: You learn something new every day.

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: [player name]! I hear you fetch mighty army for us!

chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
chatting-before-the-final-battle-talking.text: You go take them to Herr Caranos quickly!

the-final-battle.speaker: Herman Caranos
the-final-battle.text: [player name] - have you brought an army?

the-final-battle.player: No, really, the wizard told me he'd put bone seeds in this pot, and when I opened it the army would come forth from the bone seeds.

the-final-battle.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle.text: Hmmmph. I don't much like the sound of this. I certainly won't be sending anyone to Frumscone for help again!

the-final-battle.speaker: Herman Caranos
the-final-battle.text: You can talk about that later! Now we've got an army we can get on with beating the trolls!

the-final-battle.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle.text: Well, I suppose so. [player name], this could be VERY dangerous. Do you feel ready to fight?

the-final-battle.player: Aren't you going to do the fighting?

the-final-battle.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle.text: Yes, of course. But you, my trusty sidekick, are in this adventure with me, and if I'm going forth into battle, you should make sure you're ready too.

steps.player: I'm ready. Let's fight!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Good. May this, my final adventure, end well!
Cutscene begins

options.text: I'd like to get some stuff together first.

steps.player: I'd like to get some stuff together first.

steps.speaker: Herman Caranos
steps.text: Come back to us as soon as you're ready.

the-final-battle-final-battle-cutscene.text: A cutscene opens by showing the player opening the jar, causing an army of skeleton magi to appear and fight off the incoming sea trolls.
A sea troll general appears from the ocean.
The Wise Old Man does battle with the sea troll general, deftly avoiding its strikes before finishing it off with his powerful magic.
A spell flies in from off-screen, hitting the Wise Old Man, knocking him to the ground. The Sea Troll Queen appears.

the-final-battle-final-battle-cutscene.speaker: Wise Old Man
the-final-battle-final-battle-cutscene.text: I... can't... move... [player name], you must fight this for me...

the-final-battle-entering-the-colony-wit.prompt: Do you need to see the battle again?

options.text: Yes, I missed it. Show me the battle again.
No, I'm ready to move on with the quest.

steps.text: The player is transported in front of the queen.

finishing-up-after-killing-the-sea-troll.player: Now I've killed that THING, Herman's sure to reward me!

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.text: You kick big troll queenie pretty hard, ja?

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.player: Yes, I don't think you'll have any more trouble with the trolls in future.

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.text: Piscatoris Colony owe you big-time for your help. You go see Hermie - maybe he got something for you.

finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.speaker: Arnold Lydspor
finishing-up-talking-to-arnold.text: Herr Herman Caranos. I call him 'Hermie' when him not listening. Sometimes I call him worse things, but not today.

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.text: I say, you certainly gave that Troll Queen a good thrashing!

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.player: Yes, no more trouble from her.

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.speaker: Franklin Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.text: I think Herman would like to talk to you in his office. We all owe you so much.

finishing-up-talking-to-franklin.player: Ok, I'll go and see Herman.

finishing-up-talking-to-ramara-du-croiss.speaker: Ramara du Croissant
finishing-up-talking-to-ramara-du-croiss.text: [player name]? Monsieur Caranos wishes to see you in 'is office. Please, go to 'im!

finishing-up-talking-to-everyone-else.speaker: Everyone else
finishing-up-talking-to-everyone-else.text: [player name]? Mr Caranos said he wanted to see you in his office. I wouldn't keep him waiting if I were you!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: I've defeated the Sea Troll Queen!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Your fight was truly magnificent, [player name]! Congratulations!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: [player name], how can I ever thank you? You have saved my Fishing Colony from utter destruction!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Well, you mentioned something about a reward?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Of course, of course!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: I think you've earned a little something from me, too.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Ooh, goody! Thanks, old man! Um... can I have your hat?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: 'Old man'... yes, I am old. That creature nearly killed me - I have never been so close to defeat.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Aww, cheer up - we won! But can I have your hat as my reward?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Yes, we won... YOU won... It is definitely time I retired.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: So that's the end of your adventuring? Also, how about that hat of yours?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Well, I'm sure I'll find some way to keep myself busy. But yes, this has been my last quest. My swan song.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: It's been... nice working with you! It'd be even nicer if you'd give me that hat...

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Wise Old Man
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: It's been a pleasure working with you too. Do pop in to see me in Draynor soon! I leave you with my blessing...
The Wise Old Man teleports away.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Oh, he's gone. I hope he enjoys his retirement.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: HE DIDN'T GIVE ME HIS HAT!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Player performs the Cry emote.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: It's only a hat!
Player performs the Headbang emote.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Anyway, you were going to reward me too?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Oh yes, of course! You are hereby welcome to visit the Piscatoris Fishing Colony at any time and make full use of our fishing spots!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Why is it better to fish here than in Catherby or the Fishing Guild?

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Ah, I'm glad you asked that! You see, this is the only known place where you can catch monkfish!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Ok, so I can catch monkfish. Um... thanks?!

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Yes - there's good eating on a monkfish. They heal more health than the swordfish and lobsters most adventurers carry around, but they're easier to catch than sharks.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: I suppose that could be useful.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Indeed! I'm sure Arnold will help you send your monkfish to your bank account. Also, seaweed accumulates in the nets down by the shore, which you might find useful. Franklin says it's much quicker than trying to gather it on Entrana.

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.player: Maybe if I ever want to do glassblowing again...

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: Finally, I'd like to give you a little token of my thanks.
25000 Coins

finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.speaker: Herman Caranos
finishing-up-talking-to-herman-one-last-.text: No, thank YOU!
Congratulations! Quest complete!

jump-9e094655cea5ece8.player: I'll leave you to it, then.

steps.player: Could you tell me about the Wilderness, please?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If Entrana is a land dedicated to the glory of Saradomin, the Wilderness is surely the land of Zamorak.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It's a dangerous place, where adventurers such as yourself may attack each other, using all their combat skills in the struggle for survival.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: The Wilderness has different levels. In a low level area, you can only fight adventurers whose combat level is close to yours.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But if you venture into the high level areas in the far north, you can be attacked by adventurers who are significantly stronger than you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Of course, you'd be able to attack considerably weaker people too, so it can be worth the risk.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you dare to go to the far north-west of the Wilderness, there's a building called the Mage Arena where you can learn to summon the power of Saradomin himself!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Yes please.
Thanks, maybe some other time.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: As you wish. Farewell, [player name].

steps.player: What can you tell me about jungles?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If it's jungle you want, look no further than the southern regions of Karamja.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Once you get south of Brimhaven, the whole island is pretty much covered in exotic trees, creepers and shrubs.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: There's a small settlement called Tai Bwo Wannai Village in the middle of the island. It's a funny place; the chieftain's an unfriendly chap and his sons are barking mad.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Honestly, one of them asked me to stuff a dead monkey with seaweed so he could EAT it!
If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Yes, I've met them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Further south you'll find Shilo Village. It's been under attack by terrifying zombies in recent months, if my sources are correct.
If the player has completed Shilo Village:

steps.player: I've dealt with them, although there are a few still knocking about.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: The jungle's filled with nasty creatures. There are vicious spiders that you can hardly see before they try to bite your legs off, and great big jungle ogres.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: Tell me about what's underground.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh, the dwarven realms?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, there was a time, back in the Fourth Age, when we humans wouldn't have been able to venture underground. That was before we had magic; the dwarves were quite a threat.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Still, it's much more friendly now. You can visit the vast dwarven mine if you like; the entrance is on the mountain north of Falador.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you go further west you may be able to visit the dwarven city of Keldagrim. But they were a bit cautious about letting humans in, last time I asked.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: On the other hand, if you go west of Brimhaven, you'll find a huge underground labyrinth full of giants, demons, dogs and dragons to fight. It's even bigger than the caves under Taverley, although the Taverley

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: dungeon's pretty good for training your combat skills.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What mystical realms can I visit?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, you've been to Zanaris. I met a fairy years ago who said she lived there. She was an incredible warrior, considering that she wasn't even a metre tall.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Also, in my research I came across ancient references to some kind of Abyss. Demons from the Abyss have already escaped into this land; Saradomin be thanked that they are very rare!
If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

steps.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What's the biggest monster in the world?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: There's a mighty fire-breathing dragon living underground in the deep Wilderness, known as the King Black Dragon. It's a fearsome beast, with a breath that can poison you, freeze you to the ground or

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: incinerate you where you stand.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But even more deadly is the Queen of the Kalphites. As if her giant mandibles of death were not enough, she also throws her spines at her foes with deadly force. She can even cast rudimentary spells.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Some dark power must be protecting her, for she can block attacks using prayer just as humans do.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Another beast that's worthy of a special mention is the Shaikahan. It dwells in the eastern reaches of Karamja, and is almost impossible to kill except with specially prepared weapons.
If the player has completed Tai Bwo Wannai Trio:

steps.player: Actually, that one's dead. I've been helping a barmy hunter who'd sworn to kill it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.text: Poison and how to survive it

steps.player: What does poison do?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Many monsters use poison against their foes. If you get poisoned, you will not feel it at the time, but later you will begin to suffer its effects, and your life will drain slowly from you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Over time the effects dwindle to nothing, but if you had already been wounded you might die before they wear off completely.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Fortunately, followers of Guthix have devised potions that can cure the poison or even give immunity to it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Should you wish to use poison against your own enemies and those of our Lord Saradomin, there is a potion that you can smear on your daggers, arrows, spears, javelins and throwing knives.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What monsters drop good items?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: As a general rule, tougher monsters drop more valuable items. But even a lowly hobgoblin can drop valuable gems; it just does this extremely rarely.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you can persuade the Slayer Masters to train you as a Slayer, you will be able to fight certain monsters that drop valuable items far more often.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You might care to invest in an enchanted dragonstone ring. These are said to make a monster drop its most valuable items a little more often.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are these strange monsters that keep appearing out of nowhere and attacking me when I'm training?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, I imagine you see a lot of those.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Creatures such as the rock golem, river troll and tree spirit dwell in places where adventurers frequently go to train their skills. While you're training you will often disturb one by accident. It will then get angry and

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: attack you. The safest way to deal with them is to run away immediately, but they sometimes drop valuable items if you kill them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I heard that Gielinor has three gods.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed. This is correct: Saradomin, Guthix and Zamorak.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Saradomin, the great and glorious, gives life to this world.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Zamorak craves only death and destruction.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Guthix, calling itself a god of 'balance', holds no allegiance, but simply aids whatever cause suits its shifting purpose.
If the player has completed The Dig Site:

steps.player: So who's Zaros?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.player: I discovered a buried altar to a god called Zaros.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Please, do not speak further of this. No good can come of meddling in such things.

steps.player: So Zaros is real?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, my patience is limited. Speak to me no further of this - this - this foolishness.
If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!
If the player has completed Temple of Ikov but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: I've heard of another god, called Armadyl.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What is this of which you speak?

steps.player: A strange man asked me to go into the Temple of Ikov and steal the Staff of Armadyl.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: And what makes you believe in this 'Armadyl'?

steps.player: Well, there were servants of Armadyl living down in the depths of the temple. They'd been there for generations, guarding the staff.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So you trusted the word of these people who had been sitting down a hole all their lives?

steps.player: Um... Yes, I suppose so.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I wouldn't worry about this sacred 'armadyllo' anymore. Just another foolish myth.
(If the player with the Guardians of Armadyl:)

steps.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That is an impressive feat, adventurer. Truly you must be beloved in the eyes of Saradomin.
(If the player sided with Lucien:)

steps.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: YOU'VE DONE WHAT?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.
If the player has completed Icthlarin's Little Helper but not Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: How about Tumeken, Elindis, Icthlarin and the Devourer?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: What names are these?

steps.player: Down in Sophanem, they've got a chief god named Tumeken, plus a fertility goddess named Elindis. Icthlarin is their god of the dead and the Devourer...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, what folly leads you to think any of these - things, exist?

steps.player: But I've met Icthlarin! He'd got a jackal's head!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It is hot in that land, and the heat can affect a traveller in strange ways. Tell me, when you met 'Icthlarin', had you been feeling at all unwell?

steps.player: Well, now you mention it, I'd just been hypnotised by a weird woman I met in the desert.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So a strange woman interfered with your mind, then you met a man with the head of a jackal, and you decided he must be a god?

steps.player: Umm...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, make sure you don't get hypnotised again, and I'm sure you'll not meet any more jackal-headed men claiming to be gods!

steps.player: But...?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: It'd probably be best if you don't go there again.

steps.player: But you've been all around that area, haven't you? When you were travelling?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Indeed, I have.

steps.player: So you'd know all about their gods?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I know what I know.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: And knowing what I know, I do not speak of this matter. Perhaps you would be wise to heed my example.

steps.player: I wanna know about the wars of the gods!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ah, that was a terrible time. The armies of Saradomin fought gloriously against the minions of Zamorak, but many brave warriors and noble cities were overthrown and destroyed utterly.
If the player has completed Shadow of the Storm:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You have visited Uzer, and seen for yourself the damage that could be wrought by an elder-demon in its wrath.

steps.player: How did it all end?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Before the Zamorakian forces could be utterly routed, Lord Saradomin took pity on them and the battle- scarred world, and allowed a truce.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: What are the Mahjarrat?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Very little is written about the tribe of the Mahjarrat. They are believed to be from the realm of Freneskae, or Frenaskrae - the spelling in this tongue is only approximate.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: One of them, the foul Zamorak, has achieved godhood, although none knows how this came about.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Other Mahjarrat who have been particularly active upon this plane are Hazeel, Lucien, Azzanadra and Zemouregal.
If the player sided with the cultists in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: Hazeel will rise again, you'll see!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Adventurer, your actions fill me with concern!
If the player sided with Ceril in Hazeel Cult:

steps.player: I've foiled a dastardly Zamorakian plot to have Hazeel resurrected.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So I'd heard. Lord Saradomin is smiling on you.
If the player sided with the Guardians of Armadyl in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've defeated Lucien.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Truly, your bravery exceeds your stature. But I fear his defeat will not be permanent.
If the player sided with Lucien in Temple of Ikov:

steps.player: I've met Lucien. He paid me very nicely for bringing him a staff he wanted.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Traveller, I beg of you, do not have further dealings with such creatures! You do not know their power as I do.
If the player has completed Desert Treasure I:

steps.player: Azzanadra taught me some ancient magical powers after I unlocked the pyramid where he had been trapped.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.

options.text: Wielding the power of the gods

steps.player: Can I wield the power of Saradomin myself?

steps.text: If the player has completed Mage Arena I:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I see you are already learning to summon the power of Saradomin.
If the player hasn't completed Mage Arena I:

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: If you travel to the Mage Arena in the north-west reaches of the Wilderness, the battle mage Kolodion may be willing to let you learn to summon the power of Saradomin, should you be able to pass his test.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

steps.player: I want to ask you about your hat.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Why, thank you! I rather like it myself.
If the player has not yet seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

steps.player: Did you steal it from the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Me? Steal from the bank? Whatever do you mean?

steps.player: There's been a break-in at Draynor Bank, and I bet you did it.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh my goodness, what in the world could make you think I did such a thing?

steps.player: Well, you've been sitting here looking at the bank ever since you moved into this house. Now someone's robbed the bank, and suddenly your house is full of expensive stuff!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh dear, oh dear...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So what do you think I did? March across the street, smash the bank wall, knock out the bankers and steal all the money?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I'm an old man! I walk with a stick! How could I possibly have done that?

steps.player: So you didn't rob the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Just run along now, be a good lad, and don't worry yourself about me or my finances!

steps.player: Hmmm... But I'll be keeping an eye on you.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.text: If the player has seen the recording of the Draynor Bank Robbery:

options.text: You stole it off that woman in the bank!

steps.player: You stole it off that woman in the bank! You stole all this valuable stuff too!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Stole it? How could you possibly think I did such a thing?

steps.player: I saw you robbing the bank! You killed all those people!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Deary me, [player name], your imagination is running wild! What could make you think you saw me do that?

steps.player: I've seen a security recording that shows you robbing the bank. The bank's guard showed it to me.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You've seen the bank's security recording?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Tut tut tut... Oh well, at least you'll never be able to tell the bank about me. They'll never listen.

steps.player: So you're just going to get away with it?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: That's my plan, yes.

steps.player: But that's... well, it's WRONG!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Wrong? WRONG? I'll tell you what's wrong!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've spent my whole life travelling the world, doing quests for people, saving lives, saving villages from terrifying monsters and all that sort of thing.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now I'm old, and where do I have to live? In this freezing old house next to a pig-sty, with a bunch of yobs outside who can't keep their hands off the market stalls! What sort of reward is that?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: So don't talk to me about right and wrong!

steps.player: Maybe someone SHOULD talk to you about right and wrong...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Bah!

steps.player: Hmmph!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

steps.player: How can I get a hat like that?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You could buy one off another player, or wait until they're next made available by the Council.

steps.player: Can I buy your hat?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Ohhh no, I don't intend to part with this. Would you like to ask me about something else?

options.text: You should give it back, you know.
You should give it back, you know.

steps.player: You should give it back, you know.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, I think I'll keep it.

steps.player: But...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Now you've got that off your chest, would you like to ask me about anything else?

options.text: How can I get a hat like that?
How can I get a hat like that?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: That was quite an exciting quest we did together!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Oh yes, it was certainly a fitting end to my adventuring days. Your fight against the Sea Troll Queen was highly impressive!

steps.player: Are you tempted to go on another quest in the future?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, I feel I am a bit old for that kind of thing now. New times need new heroes, and I'm sure you'll always be there to answer the call!

steps.player: I'll certainly see what I can do!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

options.condition: If the player has completed Swan Song:

steps.player: When we finished fighting those sea trolls, you said you'd finished with adventuring, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Yes, that's right. I'm an old man, there's no denying it, and I need a nice quiet retirement.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Besides, I think you've proved that the new generation has its own heroes and adventurers - I should step back and let you get on with it!

steps.player: Does this mean you're not going to do any more big robberies?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well, since you saved my life when we were fighting the Sea Troll Queen, I don't mind telling you... I trust you won't tell anyone about this?

steps.player: Go on...

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I might just have something in mind. After all, that little bank incident went very smoothly.

steps.player: But you're retired!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I retired from adventuring and questing. The episode in the bank was hardly a quest, more like a shopping trip!

steps.player: Your shopping trip killed 3 bank staff and several innocent bystanders, not to mention the watchman!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I've saved countless villages from unspeakable terrors and slain innumerable evil monsters - surely I deserve some sort of reward in return? Yet what did I get? NOTHING!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You yourself would get pretty angry if you did a long and dangerous quest and didn't get any reward from it, eh? I'm sure you would!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Well imagine how I felt at the end of a long life of questing when was left penniless, and I had to move into this thief-infested village! This little shack was falling apart when I arrived!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: You go speak to that hag who keeps looking through my window - she'll show you how it used to look before I could afford to redecorate it!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Being noble and virtuous simply doesn't put food on the table, and I don't intend to sit in banks begging like so many people do these days.

steps.player: So all those quests in the past, when you saved people from monsters and stuff like that... You only helped them because you wanted a reward?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: No, it wasn't always like that. I used to be satisfied just knowing that I'd helped, and that was reward enough.

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: But eventually I realised that people forgot about me as soon as the danger was gone, and I wasn't even getting paid properly for my services. Sometimes they offered training in the various skills, but that's no use to me!

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: I eventually realised that the only way I could get a proper reward for my life's efforts is if I took the reward myself. So I took up my cape and staff and headed for the bank.

steps.player: And now you're planning to do another robbery? Didn't you get enough from the bank?

steps.speaker: Wise Old Man
steps.text: Perhaps not... But enough of this matter! Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

Ds2B1E.player: I've been through a portal into the lair of some ancient demon. It was in the city of Uzer.

Ds2B1E.speaker: Wise Old Man
Ds2B1E.text: Ah, Uzer. A city much favoured by Saradomin, destroyed by Thammaron, the elder-demon, late in the Third Age.

Ds2B1E.player: Yeah, there isn't much left there.

dsGd7p.player: That feline statue you've got on your bookshelf there - I'm sure I saw something like that when I was in Sophanem.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: I've always liked to collect little trinkets to remind me of the time when my life was more - ah - exciting.

dsGd7p.player: So you've spoken to the Sphinx, then?

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Spoken to a sphinx, you say? My dear young lady, you can't possibly be serious!

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Ha ha ha! The people who live deep in the shifting sands of the desert will often tell travellers tall tales of strange beasts, but that doesn't mean any of it's remotely true!

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Please, adventurer, there is nothing to be gained by interfering in matters you do not understand.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Even if such a creature were to exist...

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: EVEN IF SUCH A CREATURE WERE TO EXIST it would be terribly dangerous for you to get involved in its business.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: I have heard of terrible things happening to travellers in that land, and I would not wish for you to be dragged into anything like that.

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: Indeed, I have heard of adventurers doing the most shameful and blasphemous deeds believing themselves to be acting on behalf of some false god!

dsGd7p.speaker: Wise Old Man
dsGd7p.text: So please do not speak to me of this matter again. Now, I believe I was telling you of my adventurous youth...

0keLec.player: Does that mean I shouldn't ask you about the ancient magicks I learnt in that pyramid north of Sophanem?

0keLec.speaker: Wise Old Man
0keLec.text: ENOUGH! Begone from me, you foul trickster!

8-MPbm.player: Oh well, the servants rewarded me very kindly for defeating Lucien for them.

8-MPbm.speaker: Wise Old Man

iPpubb.player: It's lucky there's no Armadyl! I've pinched his staff and given it to Lucien.

iPpubb.speaker: Wise Old Man
iPpubb.text: Adventurer, I beg of you, do not meddle in the gods' affairs. No good can come of it.

0d0Vy3.speaker: Wise Old Man
0d0Vy3.text: Leave me, traveller; I am old, and your words fill me with horror.
